_doc: Revert-verify mutants for requirement c0122d7f-1c48-4bc7-b0b8-02dc109b16c4 (ticket ff7709cb, PR #4344) — the `createdInstance` substitution token, EXECUTOR side: the four-level thread (executeComposite -> executeStep -> execute -> executeCreateInstance -> ResolverContext), the value-only inheritance into a nested composite, the null=skip negative control, and the `substituteVariables` guard. Run from the repo root after replacing the path placeholders: python3 ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file>. Axis names are A<N>, matching the test titles.

_note_control_axes: КОНТРОЛЬНЫЕ ОСИ БЕЗ МУТАНТА — ЭТО ИХ ПРОДУКТ, А НЕ ДЫРА (§A118). A2b и A4 не краснеют ни у одного мутанта этого набора НАМЕРЕННО: их предмет — не гвард req c0122d7f, а (A2b) ЖИВОСТЬ ФИКСТУРЫ PropertyDefault-пути, то есть доказательство, что отсутствие свойства в A2 есть `null` резолвера, а не мёртвый путь записи; и (A4) РАЗЛИЧЕНИЕ ПОНЯТИЙ значение-против-цели, то есть что шаг пишет свой новый файл, а не в созданный ранее. Мутант на них потребовал бы ломать ЧУЖОЙ механизм (ветку `target` / таргетинг шага), который этот PR не трогает. ⛔ Не городить мутанта на контрольную ось: её зелень при мутациях предмета и есть её вердикт.

M1_composite_to_step._note: Level 1 of the thread: executeComposite stops passing what an earlier step created into executeStep. ⛤ Also reddens A10 (measured 2026-10-02, issue #4521 — NOT a silently appended axis): this mutant cuts the thread at a level ABOVE the fifth signature, and a workflow_transition's postAction receives its createdInstancePath from the very same `execute(...)` argument, so severing any earlier level starves BOTH the direct step (A1/A3) and the postAction (A10). That is a property of the LEVELS' ORDER, not a weakness of A10: the mutant that isolates the fifth signature alone is M12_postaction_forward, and it reddens A10 and nothing else.

M2a_step_to_execute._note: Level 2 of the thread: executeStep stops forwarding the created path into execute. ⛤ Also reddens A10 (measured 2026-10-02, issue #4521 — NOT a silently appended axis): this mutant cuts the thread at a level ABOVE the fifth signature, and a workflow_transition's postAction receives its createdInstancePath from the very same `execute(...)` argument, so severing any earlier level starves BOTH the direct step (A1/A3) and the postAction (A10). That is a property of the LEVELS' ORDER, not a weakness of A10: the mutant that isolates the fifth signature alone is M12_postaction_forward, and it reddens A10 and nothing else.

M3_execute_to_createinstance._note: Level 3 of the thread: execute stops forwarding the created path into executeCreateInstance. ⛤ Also reddens A10 (measured 2026-10-02, issue #4521 — NOT a silently appended axis): this mutant cuts the thread at a level ABOVE the fifth signature, and a workflow_transition's postAction receives its createdInstancePath from the very same `execute(...)` argument, so severing any earlier level starves BOTH the direct step (A1/A3) and the postAction (A10). That is a property of the LEVELS' ORDER, not a weakness of A10: the mutant that isolates the fifth signature alone is M12_postaction_forward, and it reddens A10 and nothing else.

M4_ctx_field._note: Level 4 of the thread: the ResolverContext is built without the createdInstancePath field. ⛤ Also reddens A10 (measured 2026-10-02, issue #4521 — NOT a silently appended axis): this mutant cuts the thread at a level ABOVE the fifth signature, and a workflow_transition's postAction receives its createdInstancePath from the very same `execute(...)` argument, so severing any earlier level starves BOTH the direct step (A1/A3) and the postAction (A10). That is a property of the LEVELS' ORDER, not a weakness of A10: the mutant that isolates the fifth signature alone is M12_postaction_forward, and it reddens A10 and nothing else.

M12_postaction_forward._note: The FIFTH signature on the thread: executeWorkflowTransition forwards the created path into each postAction's `this.execute(...)`. Dropping the argument compiles (the 5th parameter is optional), so the mutation is type-preserving and the postAction runs with no createdInstancePath — its `createdInstance` PropertyDefault entry is then silently skipped. ⛤ Issue #4521: the PREVIOUS M12 only INSERTED A COMMENT line above the existing one and changed no code at all — it was vacuous by construction (ITRV §A12 / §A125), so its `"expect": []` certified a NON-mutant as a measured zero. It declared an empty red set because at the time this level had NO axis (ITRV §A130: the axis was absent, not the mutant weak). A10 is that axis; the mutation is now real and the expectation is MEASURED.

_note_M12: M12 locks the FIFTH signature (workflow_transition postAction). ⛤ Its predecessor `M12_UNCOVERED_postaction_forward` declared `"expect": []` and was REFUSED by mutant-driver.py for carrying no `_canary` (issue #4521). ⛔ Attaching a canary would have been the WRONG fix: that mutant's `to` only inserted a comment line and changed no code, so a canary would have certified a non-mutant as a re-measured zero — worse than the rc=2 it caused. Two measurements, 2026-10-02, this tree: (1) the comment-only mutant is vacuous by construction; (2) a trial mutation that REALLY drops the forward reddened NO axis either — i.e. ITRV §A130, the axis was ABSENT. The axis (A10) is now written (`GroundingExecutor.createdInstanceToken.test.ts`) and the mutant is a real, type-preserving drop of the argument; its expectation is MEASURED, not declared. The `_UNCOVERED_` marker is gone from the name because the level is no longer uncovered.
_note_A10: A10 (added 2026-10-02, issue #4521) locks the FIFTH signature of the thread — a workflow_transition step's postAction. Because it sits at the END of the chain, every mutant that cuts an EARLIER level (M1, M2a, M3, M4) reddens it as well; the per-mutant `_note`s say so explicitly. The mutant that isolates this level is M12_postaction_forward → ['A10'] alone. ⛔ M2b (step → NESTED composite) and M6 (value-inheritance fallback) do NOT redden A10: they cut branches a workflow_transition step never travels, which is why their red sets are unchanged.
